revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Average Monthly Temperatures
revealWordProblem.text: The box plots show the average monthly temperatures for the same month in Chicago, IL, and Honolulu, HI. How do the monthly temperatures between the two cities compare?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Chicago's five-number summary is about Min = 26°F, Q1 = 34°F, Median = 57°F, Q3 = 74°F, Max = 90°F, giving a range of 90 − 26 = 64°F and an IQR of 74 − 34 = 40°F. Honolulu's five-number summary is about Min = 78°F, Q1 = 82°F, Median = 84°F, Q3 = 86°F, Max = 89°F, giving a range of 89 − 78 = 11°F and an IQR of 86 − 82 = 4°F. Honolulu's median (84°F) is 84 − 57 = 27°F warmer than Chicago's (57°F), and Honolulu's temperatures are far more consistent (range 11°F, IQR 4°F) than Chicago's, which swing widely across the year (range 64°F, IQR 40°F) — showing Chicago has hot summers and cold winters while Honolulu stays warm and steady year-round.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — What is a box plot?
conceptIntro.intro: A box plot is a simple picture that shows how a set of data is spread out, using just five key numbers: the lowest value, the first quartile (Q1), the median (middle), the third quartile (Q3), and the highest value. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The box always holds the middle 50% of the data, and the line inside the box is the median.

iDo.title: Watch me build one
lines: My data, in order: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22, 24, 28. There are 11 numbers.
The middle number is the 6th one, 14, so the median = 14.
The lower half is 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Its middle is 8, so Q1 = 8.
The upper half is 15, 18, 22, 24, 28. Its middle is 22, so Q3 = 22.
The lowest is 4 and the highest is 28. I draw a box from 8 to 22, a line at 14, and whiskers out to 4 and 28.

weDo.title: Let's try one together

The lower half is 2, 5 and the upper half is 8, 11. What is Q1? What is Q3?
What are the lowest and highest values? Now picture the box stretching from Q1 to Q3 with the median line inside.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

discourse.prompt: The IQR is Q3 − Q1 = 26 − 10 = 16. What does this tell you about the middle 50% of scorers?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The middle 50% of players scored between ___ and ___ points. The IQR of ___ means the middle half of the data is spread across ___ points. This tells me ___.

approaching.stem: A box plot shows: Min = 10, Q1 = 15, Median = 20, Q3 = 28, Max = 35. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
choiceFeedback: This is the spread, but IQR is Q3 − Q1 only.
Full range from min to max is 25, but IQR is different.
IQR only uses the quartiles, not min and max.
hints: You're given five numbers, but IQR only uses two of them: Q1 and Q3. Ignore the min, median, and max.
IQR = Q3 − Q1. Find Q3 (28) and Q1 (15) in the summary — the IQR is their difference, the width of the box.
Set up the subtraction Q3 − Q1: that's 28 − 15. The difference you get is the IQR.
approaching.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja muestra: Mín = 10, Q1 = 15, Mediana = 20, Q3 = 28, Máx = 35. ¿Cuál es el rango intercuartílico (RIC)?
hintsEs: Te dan cinco números, pero el RIC solo usa dos: Q1 y Q3. Ignora el mínimo, la mediana y el máximo.
RIC = Q3 − Q1. Halla Q3 (28) y Q1 (15) en el resumen: el RIC es su diferencia, el ancho de la caja.
Plantea la resta Q3 − Q1: eso es 28 − 15. La diferencia que obtengas es el RIC.

approaching.stem: On a box plot, what does the line inside the box represent?
approaching.explanation: The line inside the box of a box plot always represents the median.
choiceFeedback: The line shows center—but mean is a different measure.
The line is always the middle value, not an average.
The range is a spread — the whole distance from the smallest value to the largest — not a single line drawn inside the box. Think about which value splits the data in half.
hints: Picture a box plot: a box with whiskers, and a line cutting through the box. That line marks the CENTER of the data.
The box runs from Q1 to Q3, so the line inside splits the middle 50% in half. Think about which measure splits ordered data into halves.
First step: recall which measure means 'the middle value of the ordered data.' The line inside the box always marks that exact measure.
approaching.stemEs: En un diagrama de caja, ¿qué representa la línea que está dentro de la caja?
approaching.explanationEs: La línea dentro de la caja de un diagrama de caja siempre representa la mediana.
hintsEs: Imagina un diagrama de caja: una caja con bigotes y una línea que atraviesa la caja. Esa línea marca el CENTRO de los datos.
La caja va de Q1 a Q3, así que la línea de adentro parte por la mitad al 50% central. Piensa qué medida divide en mitades los datos ordenados.
Primer paso: recuerda qué medida significa 'el valor del medio de los datos ordenados'. La línea dentro de la caja siempre marca esa medida.

approaching.stem: What percentage of data falls between Q1 and Q3 on a box plot?
approaching.explanation: The box in a box plot contains the middle 50% of the data (from Q1 to Q3).
choiceFeedback: The box shows the inner half—is it 25%?
Q1 to Q3 is the middle section—what fraction is that?
Each quarter is 25%—Q1 to Q3 is two quarters.
hints: Quartiles cut the data into 4 equal parts — 'quart' like 'quarter.' Each part holds the same share of the data.
Each quarter of the data is 25%. Count how many quarters sit between Q1 and Q3: Q1 to the median, then the median to Q3.
First step: Q1 to the median is one quarter — 25%. Add the quarter from the median up to Q3 to get the box's total share.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué porcentaje de los datos queda entre Q1 y Q3 en un diagrama de caja?
approaching.explanationEs: La caja de un diagrama de caja contiene el 50% central de los datos (de Q1 a Q3).
hintsEs: Los cuartiles cortan los datos en 4 partes iguales: 'cuart-' como 'cuarto'. Cada parte tiene la misma porción de los datos.
Cada cuarto de los datos es 25%. Cuenta cuántos cuartos hay entre Q1 y Q3: de Q1 a la mediana y de la mediana a Q3.
Primer paso: de Q1 a la mediana es un cuarto, 25%. Suma el cuarto que va de la mediana a Q3 para obtener la porción total de la caja.

choiceFeedback: Find max and min—is range the minimum?
Max is 31, min is 8—range is the difference.
Range is spread—subtract max from min, don't add.
hints: Range = how far the data stretches: the gap between the biggest and smallest values only. The middle values don't matter.
Scan the list 14, 22, 8, 31, 17: find the maximum and the minimum, then subtract the min from the max.
First step: the max is 31 and the min is 8. Set up 31 − 8 — that difference is the range.
hintsEs: El rango es cuánto se extienden los datos: la diferencia entre el valor mayor y el menor. Los valores del medio no importan.
Revisa la lista 14, 22, 8, 31, 17: halla el máximo y el mínimo, y luego resta el mínimo del máximo.
Primer paso: el máximo es 31 y el mínimo es 8. Plantea 31 − 8: esa diferencia es el rango.

approaching.title: The Added-Quartiles IQR Mistake

workedExample.label: Box plot values
workedExample.work: Bobcats' box plot: Min = 10, Q1 = 18, Median = 24, Q3 = 30, Max = 40
workedExample.workEs: Diagrama de caja de los Bobcats: Mín = 10, Q1 = 18, mediana = 24, Q3 = 30, Máx = 40

approaching.correctWork: The IQR is Q3 MINUS Q1, not Q3 plus Q1. IQR = 30 − 18 = 12. The student added the quartiles instead of subtracting, so 48 is much larger than the actual spread of the middle 50%, which is only 12 points.
hints: IQR stands for InterQuartile RANGE — a range is found by subtracting, not adding.
approaching.titleEs: El error del IQR con cuartiles sumados
approaching.explanation: The final step added the quartiles, but a range is always a difference. The interquartile range measures how wide the box is, so IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 30 − 18 = 12: the middle 50% of the Bobcats' scores covers just 12 points, not 48.
approaching.explanationEs: El paso final sumó los cuartiles, pero un rango siempre es una diferencia. El rango intercuartílico mide qué tan ancha es la caja, así que IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 30 − 18 = 12: el 50% central de los puntajes de los Bobcats abarca solo 12 puntos, no 48.
approaching.correctWorkEs: El IQR es Q3 MENOS Q1, no Q3 más Q1. IQR = 30 − 18 = 12. El estudiante sumó los cuartiles en lugar de restarlos, así que 48 es mucho mayor que la dispersión real del 50% central, que es de solo 12 puntos.

approaching.stem: Two box plots show: Team A has IQR = 8, Team B has IQR = 22. What does this tell you?
choices: Team A's middle 50% is more consistent; Team B's is more spread out
Team B is a better team
Team A has a higher median
The IQRs don't tell you about consistency
approaching.explanation: A smaller IQR means the middle 50% of data is more tightly clustered. Team A's scoring is more consistent in the middle range.
choiceFeedback: Bigger IQR doesn't mean better—it means more variation.
IQR tells consistency—smaller is tighter.
IQR is always about consistency in the middle 50%.
hints: IQR measures the width of the box — how spread out the MIDDLE 50% of each team's scores is.
Compare a narrow box (IQR 8) with a wide box (IQR 22). Ask what narrow vs wide says about consistency — not about which team is better.
First step: translate each number — Team A's middle scores span only 8 points; Team B's span 22. Then choose the statement that matches.
approaching.stemEs: Dos diagramas de caja muestran: el equipo A tiene un RIC = 8 y el equipo B tiene un RIC = 22. ¿Qué te dice esto?
approaching.explanationEs: Un RIC más pequeño significa que el 50% central de los datos está más agrupado. La anotación del equipo A es más consistente en el rango central.
choicesEs: El 50% central del equipo A es más consistente; el del equipo B está más disperso
El equipo B es mejor equipo
El equipo A tiene una mediana más alta
Los RIC no dicen nada sobre la consistencia
hintsEs: El RIC mide el ancho de la caja: qué tan dispersos están los puntajes del 50% CENTRAL de cada equipo.
Compara una caja angosta (RIC 8) con una caja ancha (RIC 22). Pregunta qué dice angosta frente a ancha sobre la consistencia, no sobre qué equipo es mejor.
Primer paso: traduce cada número — los puntajes centrales del Equipo A abarcan solo 8 puntos; los del Equipo B abarcan 22. Luego elige el enunciado que coincida.

onLevel.title: The Quartile-Is-One-Value Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: Q1 is the MEDIAN of the lower half, not just one of its values. The lower half is 4, 8, 10, 14 — an even-sized group — so Q1 = (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9, not 10. The student grabbed a single value instead of averaging the two middle numbers of the half.
hints: When a half has an even number of values, the quartile is the average of its two middle values.
Lower half 4, 8, 10, 14: the two middle values are 8 and 10, so Q1 = (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9.
onLevel.titleEs: El error de creer que el cuartil es un solo valor
onLevel.explanation: The Q1 step grabbed a single number out of the lower half instead of finding that half's median. The lower half 4, 8, 10, 14 has an even count, so Q1 averages its two middle values: (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9 — the same averaging move already used correctly for the median and for Q3.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de Q1 tomó un solo número de la mitad inferior en vez de hallar la mediana de esa mitad. La mitad inferior 4, 8, 10, 14 tiene una cantidad par de valores, así que Q1 promedia sus dos valores del medio: (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9, el mismo procedimiento que ya se usó correctamente para la mediana y para Q3.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Q1 es la MEDIANA de la mitad inferior, no uno cualquiera de sus valores. La mitad inferior es 4, 8, 10, 14 — un grupo de tamaño par — así que Q1 = (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9, no 10. El estudiante tomó un solo valor en lugar de promediar los dos números centrales de esa mitad.

onLevel.stem: The Hawks' points per quarter are 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. Resting on the scoreboard, what are the minimum, median, and maximum?
onLevel.explanation: The data is already in order. The smallest value is 2 and the largest is 12. There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value, which is 7.
choiceFeedback: Median is the middle—with 7 values, which is in the middle?
There's no zero shown—count from the data given.
Seven values: positions 1,2,3,4,5,6,7—which is the 4th?
onLevel.stemEs: Los puntos por cuarto de los Hawks son 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. Según el marcador, ¿cuáles son el mínimo, la mediana y el máximo?
onLevel.explanationEs: Los datos ya están ordenados. El valor más pequeño es 2 y el más grande es 12. Hay 7 valores, así que la mediana es el 4.º valor, que es 7.
hints: A five-number summary always starts from a list arranged from least to greatest.
The minimum and maximum are the two ends of the ordered list; the median is the value sitting right in the middle.
There are 7 values here, so the middle one is the 4th. Count in from either end to find it.
hintsEs: Un resumen de cinco números siempre empieza con una lista ordenada de menor a mayor.
El mínimo y el máximo son los dos extremos de la lista ordenada; la mediana es el valor que queda justo en medio.
Aquí hay 7 valores, así que el del medio es el 4.º. Cuenta desde cualquiera de los extremos para hallarlo.

onLevel.stem: The Comets scored 6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34 across 8 games. After ordering, what are Q1 and Q3?
onLevel.explanation: With 8 values the median splits the data into a lower half (6, 10, 14, 18) and an upper half (22, 26, 30, 34). Q1 is the median of the lower half: (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12. Q3 is the median of the upper half: (26 + 30) ÷ 2 = 28.
choiceFeedback: First half: 6, 10, 14, 18—Q1 is the median of these.
Q1 and Q3 come from the halves—not the full data.
Split the data in half, then find median of each half.
onLevel.stemEs: Los Comets anotaron 6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34 en 8 juegos. Después de ordenarlos, ¿cuáles son Q1 y Q3?
onLevel.explanationEs: Con 8 valores, la mediana divide los datos en una mitad inferior (6, 10, 14, 18) y una mitad superior (22, 26, 30, 34). Q1 es la mediana de la mitad inferior: (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12. Q3 es la mediana de la mitad superior: (26 + 30) ÷ 2 = 28.
hints: Q1 and Q3 are medians too — one for the lower half of the data and one for the upper half.
Split the 8 ordered values into a lower half of 4 and an upper half of 4, then find the median of each half.
The lower half is 6, 10, 14, 18. With 4 values its median is the average of the middle two — work that out, then do the same for the upper half.
hintsEs: Q1 y Q3 también son medianas: una de la mitad inferior de los datos y otra de la mitad superior.
Divide los 8 valores ordenados en una mitad inferior de 4 y una mitad superior de 4, y luego halla la mediana de cada mitad.
La mitad inferior es 6, 10, 14, 18. Con 4 valores, su mediana es el promedio de los dos del centro; calcúlalo y después haz lo mismo con la mitad superior.

onLevel.stem: A box plot for the Rockets shows Min = 8, Q1 = 15, Median = 22, Q3 = 30, Max = 38. The middle 50% of their scores falls between which two values?
onLevel.explanation: The box of a box plot stretches from Q1 to Q3, and that box always holds the middle 50% of the data. Here the box goes from Q1 = 15 to Q3 = 30.
choiceFeedback: The whiskers go to min and max—but the box is 50% of data.
Q1 to median is 25%, median to Q3 is 25%—together?
Q3 to max covers another 25%—is that the middle 50%?
onLevel.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja de los Rockets muestra Mín = 8, Q1 = 15, Mediana = 22, Q3 = 30, Máx = 38. ¿El 50% central de sus puntajes queda entre qué dos valores?
onLevel.explanationEs: La caja de un diagrama de caja se extiende de Q1 a Q3, y esa caja siempre contiene el 50% central de los datos. Aquí la caja va de Q1 = 15 a Q3 = 30.
hints: In a box plot it is the box itself — not the whiskers — that holds the middle half of the data.
The box stretches from Q1 on one end to Q3 on the other.
Find Q1 and Q3 in the list of values you were given, and read off the two numbers the box runs between.
hintsEs: En un diagrama de caja es la caja misma, no los bigotes, la que contiene la mitad central de los datos.
La caja se extiende desde Q1 en un extremo hasta Q3 en el otro.
Busca Q1 y Q3 en la lista de valores que te dieron y lee los dos números entre los que va la caja.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — The Skipped Ordering Mistake

workedExample.label: Median
workedExample.work: The middle value of the list is 9, so Median = 9
workedExample.workEs: El valor en medio de la lista es 9, así que mediana = 9

workedExample.label: Q1 and Q3
workedExample.work: Lower half = 17, 5, 21 → Q1 = 5. Upper half = 13, 25 → Q3 = 25
workedExample.workEs: Mitad inferior = 17, 5, 21 → Q1 = 5. Mitad superior = 13, 25 → Q3 = 25

onLevel.correctWork: The data must be ordered from least to greatest FIRST: 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29. There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value, which is 17 (not 9). The lower half is 5, 9, 13, so Q1 = 9, and the upper half is 21, 25, 29, so Q3 = 25. The student found the 'middle of the list' without ordering the data first, which gave the wrong median and quartiles.
hints: You can never find the median or quartiles until the data is in order from least to greatest.
After ordering (5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29), the true middle value is 17, not the number that happened to sit in the middle of the unsorted list.
onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el error de saltarse el ordenamiento
onLevel.explanation: The median step used whichever number happened to sit in the middle of the unsorted list. Once the scores are ordered as 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, the 4th value is 17, so the median is 17, the lower half 5, 9, 13 gives Q1 = 9, and the upper half 21, 25, 29 gives Q3 = 25.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la mediana usó el número que por casualidad estaba en el centro de la lista sin ordenar. Una vez que los puntajes se ordenan como 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, el cuarto valor es 17, así que la mediana es 17, la mitad inferior 5, 9, 13 da Q1 = 9 y la mitad superior 21, 25, 29 da Q3 = 25.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Los datos deben ordenarse de menor a mayor PRIMERO: 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29. Hay 7 valores, así que la mediana es el 4.º valor, que es 17 (no 9). La mitad inferior es 5, 9, 13, así que Q1 = 9, y la mitad superior es 21, 25, 29, así que Q3 = 25. El estudiante buscó el 'medio de la lista' sin ordenar los datos primero, lo que dio una mediana y unos cuartiles equivocados.

onLevel.title: Find the Box Plot Error
onLevel.correctWork: Q1 is the median of the lower half (3, 7, 9), which is 7. Q3 is the median of the upper half (15, 18, 21), which is 18. The student used the wrong value for Q1 — they picked 9 (the last value in the lower half) instead of the median of that half.
hints: Q1 is not just a value in the lower half — it is the MEDIAN of the lower half.
Lower half: 3, 7, 9. The median of these three values is 7, not 9.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error del diagrama de caja
onLevel.explanation: The quartile step used 9, the last number in the lower half, instead of the middle of that half. The lower half is 3, 7, 9, so its median — and therefore Q1 — is 7. Q3 = 18 was already right, since 18 sits in the middle of 15, 18, 21.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de los cuartiles usó 9, el último número de la mitad inferior, en vez del valor del medio de esa mitad. La mitad inferior es 3, 7, 9, así que su mediana —y por lo tanto Q1— es 7. Q3 = 18 ya estaba bien, porque 18 queda en el medio de 15, 18, 21.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Q1 es la mediana de la mitad inferior (3, 7, 9), que es 7. Q3 es la mediana de la mitad superior (15, 18, 21), que es 18. El estudiante usó el valor equivocado para Q1 — tomó el 9 (el último valor de la mitad inferior) en lugar de la mediana de esa mitad.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Display Data: Box Plots is treating a quartile as just one data point instead of the median of a half — for the lower half 4, 8, 10, 14, some students pick 10 (the last value) as Q1 instead of finding the median of that half: Q1 = (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9. A second common slip is finding IQR by adding the quartiles instead of subtracting, writing IQR = Q3 + Q1 (like 30 + 18 = 48) instead of IQR = Q3 − Q1 (30 − 18 = 12) — always order the data first, then subtract Q1 from Q3 to find the spread of the middle 50%.

optionalActivity.name: Box Plot Stadium Bridge
optionalActivity.intro: Optional — one more together if the group is ready: Step onto the court and turn each team's scores into a five-number summary to power the stadium's box plot scoreboard!

diagram.title: Team B Points Per Game — Box Plot
diagram.caption: The 80 the fan brags about is a single game at the whisker's tip. Team B's box (middle half) runs 55–65 with a median of 61 — compare that to Team A's 52–68 box and median of 60.

connect.scenario: Two basketball teams' scoring data are displayed as box plots. Team A: Min=40, Q1=52, Median=60, Q3=68, Max=75. Team B: Min=35, Q1=55, Median=61, Q3=65, Max=80. A fan says Team B is better because they scored 80 points once.
connect.promptQuestion: Which team is more consistently scoring high? Use the box plot values to support your answer.
connect.prompt: Team A's IQR is ___ and Team B's IQR is ___. Team B's middle 50% scores between ___ and ___. The fan is wrong because ___. The box plot shows that Team B is more consistent because its Q1 and median are higher and its IQR (10) is smaller, while ___.

check.stem: Is the fan right that Team B is better because of the 80-point game?
choices: No — one high game is a single extreme value, not typical performance
Yes — 80 is the highest score in the data
No — Team A's maximum is higher
check.explanation: The 80 is the tip of a whisker — one game. Team B does look more consistent, but for a better reason: its middle 50% (55–65) is both higher and tighter than Team A's (52–68).

connect.modelAnswer: Team A's IQR is 68 − 52 = 16; Team B's is 65 − 55 = 10. The fan's reasoning is wrong — a single 80-point game is one extreme value at the whisker's tip, not typical performance. The conclusion happens to be right for a better reason: Team B's middle 50% of games falls between 55 and 65 with a median of 61, higher and tighter than Team A's 52–68 box with a median of 60.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: A box plot has Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 36. What is the IQR and what does it represent?
choices: IQR = 16; it is the spread of the middle 50% of the data
IQR = 56; it is the total of Q1 and Q3
IQR = 28; it is the median between Q1 and Q3
IQR = 36; it is the value of Q3
exitTicket.explanation: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 36 − 20 = 16. The IQR tells you the range of the middle 50% of the data.
choiceFeedback: IQR subtracts Q1 from Q3, it doesn't add them.
28 is the midpoint — IQR is Q3 − Q1, the spread.
36 is just Q3 — subtract Q1 to find the range between them.
hints: Two things to check in each choice: the IQR calculation AND what the IQR means. Both parts must be correct.
IQR = Q3 − Q1 — a subtraction. And it describes the spread of the middle half of the data, not a total and not a midpoint.
Set up 36 − 20, then ask: does my choice pair that difference with 'spread of the middle 50%'? Rule out any that add or average instead.

questions.stem: A runner's mile times are: 7:10, 7:15, 7:12, 7:20, 12:00. The 12:00 was due to a cramp. Which measure best represents a typical mile?
choices: Mean — it uses all the data
Mode — it shows the most common time
Median — the outlier 12:00 pulls the mean too high
questions.explanation: The 12:00 is an outlier that pulls the mean up. The median (7:15) better represents the runner's typical time.

questions.stem: Data set: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 50. The mean is about 13.8 and the median is 7. Which better represents the typical value?
choices: Median (7) — the outlier 50 inflates the mean
questions.explanation: The mean (13.8) is higher than 5 of the 6 values because the outlier 50 pulls it up. The median (7) better represents a typical value.

questions.stem: A gymnast's scores are: 8.5, 8.8, 8.7, 8.6, 8.9. There are no outliers. Which measure best represents a typical score?
choices: Neither — the data is too small
questions.explanation: The data is symmetric with no outliers, so the mean (8.7) best represents the typical score.
